name: AccI-VAD (Reiss & Hoshen, 'An Attribute-based Method for Video Anomaly Detection', TMLR 01/2025, OpenReview XL1N6iLr0G; arXiv 2212.00789v2, 26 Jan 2025)
variant_reported:
TMLR Table 2 'Ours' (micro/macro): Ped2 99.1/99.9, Avenue 93.7/96.3, ShanghaiTech 85.9/89.6. Table 3 shows which feature set produced each number:
- Ped2: velocity+CLIP gives 99.1/99.9. The paper says pose extraction is 'not feasible' on Ped2.
- Avenue: pose+CLIP+velocity gives 93.7/96.3.
- ShT: the headline mixes two rows. Micro 85.9 comes from pose+velocity with no CLIP; that row's macro is 88.8. Macro 89.6 comes from pose+CLIP+velocity, whose micro is 85.1.
The repo's evaluate.py matches this: ShT final score = velocity+pose; every other dataset = velocity+pose+deep. The arXiv v1 'Ours' row reads 99.1/99.9, 93.3/96.2, 85.9/89.6, and MULDE quotes these v1 numbers.

components.component: Object detector: detectron2 Mask R-CNN R50-FPN 3x, COCO-pretrained (config COCO-InstanceSegmentation/mask_rcnn_R_50_FPN_3x.yaml, model id 137849600, model_final_f10217.pkl). SCORE_THRESH_TEST is 0.5 for Ped2, 0.8 for Avenue and 0.8 for ShT. Extra boxes come from frame differencing plus contours (pre_processing/bboxes.py). The repo also ships precomputed boxes.
components.params_millions: Not listed by detectron2. torchvision's maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn COCO_V1 is the same R50-FPN Mask R-CNN architecture in a different implementation with a 91-class head; it lists num_params 44,401,393 (44.4M).
components.weights_mb: 177,841,981 bytes (177.8 MB) for model_final_f10217.pkl, from an HTTP HEAD that I re-ran. For reference, torchvision's checkpoint is listed as 169.8 MB.
components.gflops_per_frame: Not stated by detectron2 or AccI-VAD. torchvision lists 134.38 GFLOPS for maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn and gives no input size. Its convention is not stated, but torchvision lists ViT-B/16 at 17.56 and ResNet-50 at 4.09 GFLOPS, which suggests 1 FLOP per MAC (inferred). Runs once per frame. detectron2 MODEL_ZOO gives 0.043 s/im inference on V100.
components.source: Paper Sec. 4.2: 'We use ResNet50 Mask-RCNN ... pretrained on MS-COCO'. Repo pre_processing/object_detector.py, bboxes.py (DATASET_CFGS), pre_processing/README.md (wget URL). https://github.com/facebookresearch/detectron2/blob/main/MODEL_ZOO.md row mask_rcnn_R_50_FPN_3x: train 0.261 s/it, inference 0.043 s/im, train mem 3.4 GB, box AP 41.0, mask AP 37.2, id 137849600. https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/stable/models/generated/torchvision.models.detection.maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn.html (num_params 44401393, GFLOPS 134.38, file size 169.8 MB).

components.component: Optical flow: FlowNet2, the full stacked model from NVIDIA flownet2-pytorch (FlowNetC + 2x FlowNetS + FlowNetSD + FlowNetFusion). The checkpoint is FlowNet2_checkpoint.pth.tar, built with the default fp16=False. Frames are resized with cv2 to 1024x768 for Ped2/Avenue and 1024x640 for ShT (pre_processing/flows.py, adapted from hf2vad).
components.params_millions: 162.52M. AccI-VAD's pre_processing/flownet_networks/flownet2_models.py contains the string 'Parameter count = 162,518,834' at line 12. NVIDIA's models.py has the same string at line 28. FastFlowNet's README and paper Table III also list 162.52.
components.weights_mb: Size of AccI-VAD's Google Drive copy (id 1hF8vS6YeHkx3j2pfCeQqqZGwA_PJq_Da): not found, because the link redirects to a Google sign-in page (re-checked). NVIDIA's official FlowNet2 checkpoint is listed as '[620MB]' in the flownet2-pytorch README.
components.gflops_per_frame: At AccI-VAD's input sizes: not found. FastFlowNet (Kong et al., ICRA 2021, arXiv 2103.04524) Table III gives FlowNet2 at 24,836.4 GFLOPs at Sintel resolution, with 0.116 s on a GTX 1080Ti and 1.547 s on a Jetson TX2. The paper defines its FLOPs as 'number of floating point multiply-add operations', counted with the VCN tool. The README repeats the same figures, so the README and paper are one source from the same authors. I found no second source for this number.
components.source: Paper Sec. 4.2: 'In order to generate optical flow maps, we use FlowNet2'. Repo pre_processing/flows.py (FLOWNET_INPUT_WIDTH/HEIGHT), flownet2_models.py line 12, pre_processing/README.md. https://github.com/NVIDIA/flownet2-pytorch README line 59 ('FlowNet2 ... [620MB]'), models.py line 28. https://github.com/ltkong218/FastFlowNet README table; arXiv 2103.04524 Table III.

components.component: 2D pose: AlphaPose (cited as Fang et al. 2017 / RMPE), pretrained on MS-COCO with d = 17 keypoints, giving a 2x17 = 34-d normalised feature per human box. The exact AlphaPose model (FastPose, SimpleBaseline, HRNet, ...) is not stated, nor whether AlphaPose's own YOLOv3 detector was used. Pose features are shipped precomputed: the repo holds extracted_features/*/pose.npy, and the ShT train file is on Drive / Git LFS.
components.params_millions: Not found. Neither the paper (v1 or v2) nor the repo names the variant, and the AlphaPose MODEL_ZOO lists no parameter counts.
components.weights_mb: Not found for the variant used. For reference only: AlphaPose's default COCO model fast_res50_256x192.pth is shown as '(155M)' on its Google Drive download page (re-checked).
components.gflops_per_frame: Not found for the variant used. For reference only: AlphaPose TPAMI (arXiv 2211.03375) Table IV gives FastPose-hm ResNet-50, YOLO-v3 detector, 256x192 at 5.9 GFLOPs. Per the Table III caption, top-down GFLOPs count the pose model only and ignore the detector. The same table lists SimplePose R50 256x192 at 8.9 GFLOPs. The cost is per person crop, so the total scales with the number of persons.
components.source: Paper Sec. 4.2: 'we use AlphaPose (Fang et al., 2017) pretrained on MS-COCO with d = 17 keypoints'. Repo README: 'Pose representations have already been provided by us.' https://github.com/MVIG-SJTU/AlphaPose/blob/master/docs/MODEL_ZOO.md ; AlphaPose TPAMI arXiv 2211.03375 Tables III/IV.

components.component: Deep features: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 image encoder. models/models.py calls clip.load("ViT-B/16"), which loads the full CLIP model including the text tower. Only encode_image is called, on each object crop resized to 224x224 (video_dataset.py patch_size=224), and it outputs 512-d. On a CUDA device, OpenAI clip.load builds the model with convert_weights() (fp16) and casts to float only on CPU, so as written CLIP runs in fp16 on GPU.
components.params_millions: Image tower 86.19M; full CLIP model 149.62M. Source: OpenCLIP docs/model_profile.csv, rows ViT-B-16 (line 26) and ViT-B-16-quickgelu (line 27); the QuickGELU row matches OpenAI's activation.
components.weights_mb: 350,837,078 bytes (350.8 MB) for ViT-B-16.pt, the full CLIP model, from an HTTP HEAD of the URL at openai/CLIP clip/clip.py line 37 (re-checked).
components.gflops_per_frame: 35.13 GFLOPs per 224x224 crop for the image tower; the text tower is 5.96 (OpenCLIP model_profile.csv). The csv 'gflops' columns come from OpenCLIP's default torch profiler (profiler.py, --profiler default 'torch', torch.utils.flop_counter.FlopCounterMode), which counts 2 FLOPs per MAC, so this is about 17.6 GMACs. The cost is per object; the paper reports an average of 5 objects per frame.
components.source: Paper Sec. 4.2: 'We use a pretrained ViT B-16 CLIP ... image encoder as our deep feature extractor'. Repo models/models.py, feature_extraction.py. https://github.com/mlfoundations/open_clip/blob/main/docs/model_profile.csv ; https://github.com/mlfoundations/open_clip/blob/main/src/open_clip_train/profiler.py ; https://github.com/openai/CLIP/blob/main/clip/clip.py (line 37 URL, lines 138-141) and model.py (convert_weights).

components.component: kNN density with k=1: exact squared-L2 search with faiss IndexFlatL2 moved to GPU (index_cpu_to_gpu), over all training-object pose features (34-d) and CLIP features (512-d). This is a stored memory bank, and the frame score is the max over objects.
components.params_millions: Not applicable (non-parametric memory bank). Bank sizes are given under per_scene_artifacts.
components.weights_mb: See per_scene_artifacts.
components.gflops_per_frame: Not reported. TMLR Table 5 ('All' row, all three features) gives the kNN time as 4.93 ms/frame on Avenue and 36.0 ms/frame on ShT. With a k-means compressed bank it takes 0.51 to 0.53 ms (Avenue) and 0.45 to 0.46 ms (ShT), with a small AUROC loss.
components.source: Paper Sec. 4.2 ('kNN for the pose and deep representations with k = 1'), Table 5. Repo evaluate.py, score_calibration.py.

components.component: GMM on velocity features: an orientation histogram of optical flow per object, with B=8 bins for Avenue/ShT and B=1 for Ped2 (feature_extraction.py). Uses sklearn GaussianMixture with default full covariance. The paper says n=5; the code uses n=2 for Ped2 and n=5 otherwise. Scores are then calibrated: velocity and pose are scaled by min and 99.9th percentile, deep features by min and max of training scores. Finally a per-video, non-causal gaussian_filter1d is applied, with sigma 3 for Ped2/Avenue and 7 for ShT.
components.params_millions: Not stated. Derived from the code defaults (full covariance): 225 free values for 8-d with n=5 (5 weights + 40 means + 180 covariance entries), and 6 for 1-d with n=2. This is negligible.
components.weights_mb: Not stored. evaluate.py refits the GMM from train velocity.npy on every run.
components.gflops_per_frame: Not reported. The paper gives about 5 ms per frame for velocity, pose and deep feature extraction plus scoring.
components.source: Paper Sec. 4.2. Repo evaluate.py (GaussianMixture n_components=2 for ped2, else 5; np.percentile(...,99.9); gaussian_filter1d), feature_extraction.py (bins), README ('--sigma=3 for Ped2 and Avenue, and --sigma=7 for ShanghaiTech').

gpu_memory: Not found. The paper names the hardware ('NVIDIA RTX 2080 GPU') but reports no GPU memory figure; neither v1 nor v2 contains one.
per_scene_artifacts:
Artifacts are stored per dataset, not per scene: ShT's 13 scenes are pooled into one faiss index. Each dataset needs:
- the full training-set feature files, used as kNN banks and for GMM fitting;
- calibration score files (train_pose_scores.npy, train_deep_features_scores.npy).
Sizes of the authors' released training features (Drive folder 1vSMpDb5jIyc2tNJaYVphguUlFcwPayms), all re-checked; byte counts are from HTTP HEAD, M/G values from Drive's download-warning page:
- Avenue train: deep_features.npy 112M, pose.npy 20,501,883 B, velocity.npy 8,178,350 B.
- ShanghaiTech train: deep_features.npy 1.1G; velocity.npy 89,682,425 B; pose.npy 186M on Drive, which is exactly 194,913,310 B per the Git LFS pointer at repo extracted_features/shanghaitech/train/pose.npy (the README calls it a '195 MB npy file').
- Ped2 train: deep_features.npy 30,841,906 B, velocity.npy 382,186 B, pose.npy 4,169,122 B (on both Drive and the repo).
The files are pickled object arrays. Because CLIP runs fp16 on CUDA, deep_features.npy probably holds fp16 vectors; this is inferred from the code, not checked.
For the reported ShT micro configuration (pose+velocity), the 1.1G CLIP bank is not needed.
portability:
- Python 3.7, torch==1.12.0+cu102 (README).
- detectron2 is needed for the detector. It is installed from git and compiles its own detectron2._C C++/CUDA extension (detectron2 setup.py).
- FlowNet2 needs three custom CUDA extensions (correlation_package, resample2d_package, channelnorm_package, each with .cu kernels), built by pre_processing/install_flownet2.sh via setup.py install. flows.py calls flownet2.cuda(), so it is CUDA-only as written.
- Uses the OpenAI `clip` package (fp16 on CUDA).
- faiss-GPU is required by evaluate.py and score_calibration.py (faiss.StandardGpuResources, index_cpu_to_gpu).
- scikit-learn is used for the GMM; scipy for smoothing.
- AlphaPose code is not in the repo; only precomputed pose.npy files are provided. AlphaPose's own setup.py builds nms_cuda, roi_align_cuda, deform_conv_cuda and deform_pool_cuda (plus CPU NMS ops).
- No ONNX, TensorRT or edge export is reported in the paper or repo.
- No external APIs.
- For context, FastFlowNet Table III reports FlowNet2 at 1.547 s per Sintel-resolution pair on a Jetson TX2.
notes:
1. Which networks run at test time depends on the dataset in the reported configuration: Ped2 uses detector + flow + CLIP; Avenue uses detector + flow + AlphaPose + CLIP; ShT micro 85.9 uses detector + flow + AlphaPose, with no CLIP.
2. Code vs paper on Ped2: evaluate.py sums velocity+pose+deep for every non-ShT dataset and the repo/Drive ship a ped2 pose.npy, but the paper (Table 3 and text) reports Ped2 with velocity+CLIP only.
3. Backbone ablations: Table 6 swaps FlowNet2 for RAFT and Table 7 swaps Mask R-CNN for YOLO-v8. The reported numbers use FlowNet2 and Mask R-CNN.
4. Flow and boxes are precomputed and saved to disk as offline preprocessing.
5. FLOP conventions: OpenCLIP counts 2 FLOPs per MAC. FastFlowNet counts multiply-adds (1 per MAC). torchvision's convention is not stated, but its ViT-B/16 entry of 17.56 implies MAC-style counting (inferred).

name: MULDE, object-centric (Micorek et al., 'MULDE: Multiscale Log-Density Estimation via Denoising Score Matching for Video Anomaly Detection', CVPR 2024, pp. 18868-18877; arXiv 2403.14497)
variant_reported:
Table 1 'MULDE (ours)': Ped2 99.7/99.9, Avenue 94.3/96.1, ShT 86.7/91.5 (micro/macro). Table 1 also lists MULDE with beta=0 at 99.7/99.9, 93.1/96.1, 86.4/91.0. Supplementary Tables S3 (Avenue) and S4 (ShT) identify the feature sets:
- Avenue 94.3/96.1 = pose+deep+velocity.
- ShT micro 86.7 = P+D+V, whose macro is 90.6.
- ShT macro 91.5 = P+V, whose micro is 86.6.
So, like AccI-VAD, the headline mixes configurations. The feature set behind Ped2 99.7/99.9 is not stated.
The beta value of the object-centric 'MULDE (ours)' row is not stated explicitly. beta = 0.1 is chosen 'as a compromise' in the frame-centric ablation (Table 3).

components.component: Object detector: Mask R-CNN R50-FPN from the AccI-VAD pipeline. MULDE only says it 'detects objects in each video frame', reuses the Reiss & Hoshen extraction pipeline, and uses 'the features provided by Reiss and Hoshen'.

components.component: MULDE density network f_theta(x, sigma): an MLP of Linear(d+1, 4096)-GELU-Linear(4096, 4096)-GELU-Linear(4096, 1). The repo defaults have no LayerNorm and no dropout. The noise level is concatenated to the input. Features are standardised per component, and each feature is evaluated at L=16 evenly spaced sigmas. Per Supp. 7.2, P, D and V scores are standardised, negative values are clipped, and the results are summed. Supp. Tables S3/S4 report single-feature MULDE results, which implies one density model per feature type, though the paper never says 'three networks' explicitly.
components.params_millions:
Not reported by the authors. Exact arithmetic from the stated architecture plus the repo's d+1 input:
- deep (d=512): 18,890,753
- pose (d=34): 16,932,865
- velocity (d=8): 16,826,369
The three networks total 52,649,987. If MULDE used AccI-VAD's 1-bin Ped2 velocity features, the velocity network would be 16,797,697; MULDE does not state this. All counts are derived, not published.
components.weights_mb: Not found. No trained VAD weights are released; the repo is a 2-D toy example. Derived fp32 size is about 67.2 to 75.6 MB per network (arithmetic only).
components.gflops_per_frame: Not reported. Runtime: 'less than one millisecond to process a single feature', stated for 'the frame-centric approach with 512-dimensional feature vectors' even though the frame-centric Hiera-L features are 1152-d. Cost per object is 16 forward passes (L=16) per feature type.
components.source: MULDE Sec. 4 'Implementation details': 'two hidden layers with 4096 units followed by GELU ... final layer has an output dimension of one'; 'L = 16 evenly spaced noise levels'; 'we standardize the video features component-wise'. Supp. 7.2. Repo models.py (MLPs: layernorm=False, dropout=None; docstring 'ScoreOrLogDensityNetwork(MLPs(input_dim=d+1, output_dim=1, units=[4096, 4096]))'). https://github.com/jakubmicorek/MULDE-Multiscale-Log-Density-Estimation-via-Denoising-Score-Matching-for-Video-Anomaly-Detection

components.component: GMM over the 16-d vector of multi-scale log-densities, one per density network, fitted by EM with 1, 3 or 5 components. Scores are then temporally smoothed with a 1-D Gaussian filter. The paper does not state which component count produced Table 1. The toy repo fits covariance_type='full' for components in [1, 3, 5].
components.params_millions: Not stated. Derived for a 16-d full-covariance GMM: 153 values per component (1 weight + 16 means + 136 covariance entries). This is negligible.
components.weights_mb: not found
components.gflops_per_frame: not reported
components.source: MULDE Supp. Sec. 7.3 'Details on GMM fitting': 'fit a L-dimensional GMM with one, three, and five components'; Fig. 4. Repo main.py line ~277 (GaussianMixture(n_components=components_, covariance_type='full')).

gpu_memory: Not found. The paper names an 'NVIDIA RTX 2080Ti GPU' but reports no memory figure.
per_scene_artifacts:
Stored per dataset (no per-scene models are mentioned):
- the trained density MLPs, one per feature type used (P, D, V; inferred from Supp. 7.2). Derived fp32 sizes are about 67 to 76 MB each, arithmetic only, not reported.
- the fitted 16-d GMMs;
- per-component feature standardisation statistics and score standardisation statistics.
Unlike AccI-VAD, no training feature bank is needed for kNN at test time. However, the training inputs are AccI-VAD's released per-dataset feature files, whose sizes are in the AccI-VAD row.
portability:
- MULDE itself is a plain PyTorch MLP plus a scikit-learn GaussianMixture. The repo environment.yml pins Python 3.8.19, PyTorch 2.3.0 (cuda12.1, cudnn8.9.2) and scikit-learn 1.3.2.
- The public repo contains only the 2-D toy example (README, dataset.py, main.py, models.py, utils.py, plotting_utils.py, environment.yml): no VAD feature extraction, no Ped2/Avenue/ShT training scripts, no released weights.
- The object-centric variant inherits every dependency of the AccI-VAD pipeline: detectron2 (compiled _C), FlowNet2 with custom CUDA ops (correlation, resample2d, channelnorm), AlphaPose (its own CUDA extensions) and the OpenAI CLIP package.
- No ONNX, TensorRT or edge export is reported.
- No external APIs.
notes:
1. MULDE's Table 1 quotes AccI-VAD's arXiv-v1 numbers (Avenue 93.3/96.2), not the TMLR 93.7/96.3.
2. The test-time network stack is AccI-VAD's (Mask R-CNN + FlowNet2 + AlphaPose + CLIP ViT-B/16, the latter via AccI-VAD's code). MULDE replaces the kNN banks and the velocity GMM with noise-conditioned 2x4096 MLPs plus 16-d GMMs.
3. MLP parameter counts are exact arithmetic from the stated layers and the repo's d+1 input, not author-reported.

name: MULDE, frame-centric (Hiera-L features; same paper)
variant_reported: Table 2 / Table 3 (beta = 0.1), micro/macro: ShanghaiTech 81.3/85.9, UCF-Crime 78.5/84.9, UBnormal 72.8/85.5. With beta=0: 78.4/86.0, 75.9/84.8, 71.3/86.0. The frame-centric variant is not reported on Ped2 or Avenue.

components.component: Hiera-L video backbone, 16 frames at 224x224, 1152-d output. MULDE describes it as 'a masked autoencoder pre-trained on images and fine-tuned on Kinetics400' and does not name the checkpoint file. name: AnomalyRuler (Yang et al., Follow the Rules, ECCV 2024; github.com/Yuchen413/AnomalyRuler)
variant_reported: The Table 3 row 'AnomalyRuler' (AUC Ped2 97.9 / Ave 89.7 / ShT 85.2 / UB 71.9) uses the default setup in Sec. 5.1 'Implementation Details' (arXiv 2407.10299v2). CogVLM-17B is the VLM for visual perception, GPT-4-1106-Preview is the LLM for induction, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 is the LLM for deduction. The paper says it uses Mistral because running GPT on full test sets costs too much. Default hyperparameters are n=10 batches, m=1 normal frame per batch, majority-vote padding p=5 and EMA alpha=0.33. The 'AnomalyRuler-base' row (96.5 / 82.2 / 84.6 / 69.8) is the 'preliminary detection result' after perception smoothing (paper Sec. 4): CogVLM descriptions, then keyword matching and EMA plus majority smoothing, with no Mistral robust reasoning. The repo computes it in majority_smooth.py, which prints 'AUC for AnomalyRuler-base'. Both rows were re-checked against the arXiv v2 PDF.

gpu_memory: The paper reports no GPU memory, no hardware and no runtime. The CogVLM model card says inference needs close to 40GB VRAM, or the model must be split across GPUs with accelerate (https://huggingface.co/zai-org/cogvlm-chat-hf). In GitHub issue #5 (https://github.com/Yuchen413/AnomalyRuler/issues/5) the repo owner answered a question about GPU use and FPS. Visual perception needs at least 40GB; the authors used float16 models. A 4-bit quantized version is claimed to need 11GB. The owner also wrote 'It should be 15FPS for ShanghaiTech.' without saying what that FPS measures. No other memory or speed figure was found.
per_scene_artifacts: No trained weights. The fitted artifacts are per dataset, not per scene: one GPT-4-induced rule text file each. Sizes from the GitHub tree: rule/rule_SHTech.txt 1,988 B, rule/rule_avenue.txt 1,992 B, rule/rule_ped2.txt 2,047 B, rule/rule_UBNormal.txt 2,403 B. Deduction reads the dataset's own rule text (main.py passes rule/rule_{data}.txt to mixtral_double_deduct). The anomaly-keyword list used for perception smoothing and the initial keyword match is shared across datasets. majority_smooth.main() and mixtral_double_deduct() both load rule/rule_SHTech.npy for every dataset. If the file is missing, they fall back to the hard-coded 20-word list in majority_smooth.anomaly_keywords(), which saves rule/rule_SHTech.npy; the .npy is not in the repo. Cached CogVLM descriptions are committed in the repo as {data}/test_frame_description/*.txt: ShT 107 files (12,498,031 B), Avenue 21 (6,418,609 B), Ped2 12 (1,008,863 B), UBNormal 62 (10,079,143 B). UBNormal video test_abnormal_scene_3_scenario_3 has a frame CSV but no description. Step 3 writes the smoothed {data}/modified_test_frame_description, which is not in the repo. test.csv row counts (frames described at test time): ShT 40,791, Avenue 15,324, Ped2 2,010, UBNormal 28,175.
training_on_target: No gradient training. Induction uses a few normal training frames sampled at random from {data}/train.csv (label 0, np.random.seed(2024)). The paper default is n=10 batches of m=1 frame, so 10 frames: 10 CogVLM descriptions, 10 GPT-4 rule-generation calls and 1 GPT-4 aggregation call. The README example runs '--b=1 --bs=10' (1 batch of 10 frames), while main.py defaults to b=10, bs=1. GPU hours and API cost are not stated.
portability: README dependencies: torch 2.1.0, torchvision 0.16.0, transformers 4.35.0, accelerate 0.24.1, sentencepiece 0.1.99, einops 0.7.0, xformers 0.0.22.post7, triton 2.1.0, plus pandas, pillow, openai, scikit-learn and protobuf. There is no requirements.txt (issue #8 asks for one). openai_api.py imports inflect; every stage imports it through majority_smooth, but the README does not list it. CogVLM loads with trust_remote_code=True, and its hub code visual.py runs import xformers.ops and xops.memory_efficient_attention. image2text.py hard-codes .to('cuda') for inputs, and BART is pinned to device 0. A closed external API (OpenAI GPT-4, openai SDK plus API key) is needed for rule induction and optional keyword re-extraction. Test-time deduction is local (Mistral-7B plus BART-large-MNLI). Neither the paper nor the repo reports any ONNX, TensorRT, quantized or edge export; the only 4-bit mention is the owner's issue #5 reply. The pipeline runs offline as staged scripts over pre-extracted JPEG frames: image2text.py, then main.py --induct, then majority_smooth.py, then main.py --deduct. The README says one can start from Step 3 to reuse the rules and reproduce results; the committed descriptions make that possible without running CogVLM.
notes: CONFIRMED: the Table 3 numbers for AnomalyRuler (97.9/89.7/85.2/71.9) and AnomalyRuler-base (96.5/82.2/84.6/69.8), and the Sec. 5.1 defaults (CogVLM-17B, GPT-4-1106-Preview, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, n=10, m=1, p=5, alpha=0.33). CONFIRMED: every HF param count and file size (CogVLM 17,639,687,424 / 35,279,529,448 B; Mistral 7,241,732,096 / 14,483,498,016 B; BART 407,344,133 / 1,629,437,147 B; vicuna tokenizer.model 499,723 B), the rule-file sizes, the test.csv counts and the issue #5 quote. The listed weight files sum to about 51.4 GB; that is a sum, not a reported figure. CORRECTED: the CogVLM-paper citation. EVA2-CLIP-E use is stated in Sec. 2.1 (Architecture), not Sec. 2.2, and the 4.4B figure is in Sec. 3.5 (Ablation Study). CORRECTED: the earlier draft said the CogVLM test descriptions are not in the repo. They are committed for all four datasets (sizes in per_scene_artifacts); only modified_test_frame_description is missing. CORRECTED: the earlier draft said mixtral_double_deduct loads rule_SHTech.txt for every dataset. It loads the dataset's own rule/rule_{data}.txt; only the keyword list (rule_SHTech.npy or the hard-coded list) is shared across datasets. ADDED (code facts): majority_smooth.evaluate() calls ema_majority_smooth(..., window_size=1), which gives pad_size 0, so the released code does not use the paper's p=5 window. image2text.py get_description_frame iterates all_video_csv_paths[31:], a leftover slice that skips the first 31 videos. Final AnomalyRuler frame scores are an EWM (span=10) over binary predictions (utils.evaluate_from_result line 31). Three neural models run at test time: CogVLM-17B per frame, Mistral-7B per frame and BART-large-MNLI on negative-keyword frames. The paper never mentions BART. Issues #11 and #13 report users could not reproduce the Avenue result; #11 got AnomalyRuler-base Avenue AUC 0.724 against 82.2 in the paper. Neither issue has a maintainer reply. Issue #6 (title, in Chinese) says the README run flow differs from the paper; its body points to keyword matching repeated before robust reasoning in mixtral_double_deduct. Neither the paper nor the repo describes online or streaming operation.

name: AnyAnomaly (Ahn et al., Zero-Shot Customizable VAD with LVLM, WACV 2026; github.com/SkiddieAhn/Paper-AnyAnomaly)
variant_reported: VAD benchmark numbers come from WACV main paper Table 5: AnyAnomaly at Ave 87.3 / ShT 79.7 / UB 74.5 / UCF 80.7, and AnyAnomaly* (tested without context) at 81.4 / 77.2 / 73.1 / 77.8. Ped2 is not evaluated. Supplementary A.2 and B.3 say the VAD-dataset experiments use MiniCPM-V 8B, which Table S4 lists as 'MiniCPM-Llama3-V-2 5 (8B)'. Chat-UniVi-7B is used for the C-VAD (C-ShT / C-Ave) experiments. Settings: CLIP ViT-B/32 (A.2), window sizes (120,120)/(80,80)/(48,48) with large = (240,240) on C-Ave and Ave (A.2), and segment length 24 (Table S2, the best of 8/16/24/32 on C-VAD; the code default is clip_length=24). Fusion weights gamma1/2/3 are tuned per dataset (Supp. Table S3): Ave 0.6/0.3/0.1, ShT 0.5/0.3/0.2, UB 0.6/0.1/0.3, UCF 0.6/0.1/0.3. Main paper Sec. 4.6: each anomaly class serves as the text X and the maximum score is assigned to the segment. All experiments ran on a single RTX 3090 (Supp. A.2). The released repo contains only the C-VAD implementation, with configs for avenue and shtech and no UBnormal or UCF-Crime loader. The owner describes the benchmark protocol in issues #9 and #12. C-VAD inference runs over all test videos separately for each class. The per-frame max across classes is taken separately for the org, wa and tc streams, then the streams are fused with an optional grid search. That post-processing script is not released. For ShT the owner says inference was run 13 times, while config.py and Supp. A.1 list 11 ShT classes. The UCF-Crime test subset is listed in issue #12.

It selects patches for the temporal-context grid from the same multi-scale patches of 4 frames, plus 1 text. With class_adaption=True (the default), the text embedding is rebuilt for every keyword and segment from 21 prompt templates times every class in type_list. gpu_memory: Not reported. Supplementary A.2 says all experiments ran on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090. Component-level figures only, not reported by AnyAnomaly: the MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 model card says the int4 version needs about 8GB of GPU memory. The MiniCPM-V paper (arXiv 2408.01800, Sec. 5.2 'Basic Practice', Quantization) says the fp16 model typically demands 16~17G of memory and Q4_K_M 4-bit cuts that to about 5G. Throughput is reported only for the C-VAD experiments on the RTX 3090: Supp. Table S2 and Table S4 give Chat-UniVi-7B 6.67 FPS at segment length 24 (frame-level baseline 0.96 FPS), MiniCPM-V 2.5 1.36 FPS, Qwen2.5-VL-3B 11.18 FPS (HF) or 34.78 FPS (vLLM), and Qwen2.5-VL-7B 24.08 FPS (vLLM). The owner repeats 6.67 FPS for Chat-UniVi in issue #8. No FPS is reported for the multi-class VAD benchmark runs. Supp. D.2 says multiple abnormal events must each be processed independently, which increases latency.
per_scene_artifacts: No trained or fitted networks and no memory bank. Per-dataset items: (1) the anomaly-class text prompts. config.py type_list has 5 Ave classes and 11 ShT classes; Supp. A.1 lists 22 abnormal event types for UB and 13 anomaly categories for UCF, which have no released config. (2) Dataset-specific window sizes: large window 240 on Ave and 120 on ShT. (3) Fusion weights gamma1/2/3, tuned per dataset (Supp. Table S3), and a 1-D Gaussian smoothing sigma. The released evaluation defaults to --grid_search=True. With that default it scans sigma in [1,30) and the weights in steps of 0.1, keeping whatever maximizes AUC against the test labels (functions/eval_func.py evaluate_auc). In issue #10 the owner confirms this test-set tuning and says sigma is typically optimal within 1-20. Table S3 reports both untuned (weights 1.0/1.0/1.0) and tuned AUC, e.g. ShT 79.4 vs 79.7 and Ave 84.4 vs 87.3. The paper does not say whether sigma was fixed in the untuned rows.
training_on_target: None. The method is zero-shot: no fine-tuning of the LVLM or CLIP and no use of target training data. The only per-dataset fitting is the test-set post-processing tuning described above. GPU hours are not stated.
portability: No closed API: the repo makes no OpenAI or GPT calls, and all LVLMs are open weights run locally. requirements.txt lists h5py, fastprogress, scikit-learn, openai-clip and opencv-python==4.10.0.84. eval_func.py also imports scipy, which requirements.txt does not list. The MiniCPM variant needs the MiniCPM-V repo requirements and trust_remote_code=True. Its hub code imports only standard transformers modules (Idefics2VisionTransformer, LlamaForCausalLM) and its own resampler, with no xformers import. The Chat-UniVi variant needs the Chat-UniVi repo cloned and installed with 'pip install -e', plus numpy 1.24.3 and a git-lfs weight download. The Qwen variant needs vLLM, flash-attn, transformers installed from git, and qwen-vl-utils[decord]==0.0.8. The AnyAnomaly paper and repo report no ONNX, TensorRT or edge export. The code has an int4 MiniCPM load branch that no reported result uses. Component level only: the MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 model card reports official llama.cpp/GGUF support, ollama, an int4 version (8GB) and Qualcomm NPU (QNN) acceleration on phones; AnyAnomaly does not report using any of them. Supp. B.4 says AnyAnomaly has strong potential for real-time use, based on the C-VAD FPS with vLLM. Supp. D.2 says they adopted 'the most lightweight model among the SOTA LVLMs'.
notes: CONFIRMED: Table 5 numbers (87.3/79.7/74.5/80.7 and 81.4/77.2/73.1/77.8; no Ped2), the MiniCPM-V 8B choice (Supp. A.2/B.3/Table S4), CLIP ViT-B/32, the window sizes, the Table S3 weights and AUCs, and the RTX 3090. CONFIRMED: arXiv 2503.04504 has 4 versions; v4 is dated 5 Dec 2025, has 17 pages, and repeats Table 5 and the supplementary content. CORRECTED: the earlier draft said 'in those runs the code loops over every anomaly keyword'. The released code is C-VAD only: one keyword, or a '-'-joined --multiple list tied to the C-VAD multi-class JSON. Per the owner (issues #9 and #12), benchmark VAD was produced by running C-VAD once per class over all test videos and taking the per-frame max per stream offline. The cost is the same: 3 MiniCPM calls per class per 24-frame segment, so LVLM calls grow linearly with the number of classes. CORRECTED: the earlier draft said throughput was reported for 'a single text query'. The supplement reports C-VAD FPS without stating the number of queries. CORRECTED: the earlier draft said AnyAnomaly 'does not use' int4. The code can load an int4 checkpoint, but no reported result uses it. ADDED: clip_path_loader drops trailing frames that do not fill a 24-frame segment, and labels are truncated to match before AUC. For the cited VAD numbers, the test-time models are MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 (17.07 GB fp16) plus CLIP ViT-B/32 (0.35 GB). The segment score is copied to all 24 frames and smoothed with a 1-D Gaussian filter, and the method runs offline over pre-extracted frames.

variant_reported: Student with m=5 CvT blocks, s=5 heads and 3 output heads (Avenue/ShanghaiTech: 1x1, 4x4, 16x16; Ped2: 1x1, 30x30, 60x60), distilled from 2 teachers (T1 + T2) with standard + adversarial KD (alpha=0.1). components.component: Student: CyTran-based convolutional transformer. gpu_memory: Table 3 'Memory usage (GB)': student 6.5 vs teacher T2 17. The text calls this RAM ('consuming about one third of the RAM') and does not specify the device or the input batch.
per_scene_artifacts: One student checkpoint per dataset; trainer.py saves best_model.pkl, latest_checkpoint.pkl and periodic snapshots. Per-frame teacher anomaly maps are precomputed and stored as .npy files at 3 resolutions per teacher, for both the training and the test frames. The released test loader also loads the test-set teacher maps to log an evaluation loss. Sizes are not stated.
training_on_target: Per dataset: (1) train both object-centric teachers with their official code and run them to produce target anomaly maps. (2) Pretrain the student as an auto-encoder that reconstructs the middle frame (config_ae.json: lr 1e-3, 35 epochs, batch 48). (3) Distil for 35 epochs on mini-batches of 64 sequences of 3 frames with Adam, lr 1e-4, weight decay 1e-5 (paper). The repo's config.json instead uses batch 48, weight_decay 5e-6 and StepLR (step 10, gamma 0.5). GPU hours are not stated. The Limitations section says the teachers must be applied whenever training on a new dataset. trainer.py evaluates on the test loader every epoch and keeps best_model.pkl at the highest test micro-AUC.
portability: The student is plain PyTorch plus einops (Conv2d, BatchNorm, depthwise conv, attention via einsum), with no custom CUDA ops in the repo. The README lists Python 3.6+, PyTorch 1.2+ and the CUDA Toolkit for GPU support. Reported speeds: 1480 FPS on an 'Nvidia GeForce GTX 3090 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM' (as written) and 88 FPS on an Intel i9 3.7 GHz CPU without GPU. No ONNX, TensorRT or edge export is reported. The teacher code (lilygeorgescu/AED, AED-SSMTL) is available only on request: an academic-email form under SecurifAI's NonCommercial Use & No Sharing licence. Fast-AED code is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
